pageProps.title: Shipu Rondo
pageProps.review: This work by Keigo Higashino begins as a thriller with an intelligent criminal, but turns into a comedy through the mistakes of a clumsy middle-aged researcher, offering a unique comic irony through the resolution of the case with helpers and a hollow ending.
pageProps.content:
## Review The work intended to proceed as a thriller of a brain fight with an intelligent criminal at the beginning, but moves into the realm of unpredictable comedy.
The miscasting of a clumsy, ordinary, lethargic middle-aged researcher who took on all responsibility is used as a device for comic tension in a potentially boring case.
His clumsy and poor suspicious behavior invites suspicion from surrounding characters and constantly brings about unintended crises. In such a situation, he accidentally meets two capable helpers and solves the case.
The hollow ending, which ended as a simple happening, seems to be a device that completes the ```comic irony``` that penetrates the entire work.
